message.content: Fusion research has already improved magnetic confinement, superconducting magnets, and high-heat-flux materials, helping laboratories test extreme conditions safely. It has advanced plasma diagnostics, remote maintenance robotics, and tritium handling methods that are now useful in medical imaging and radiation facilities. Collaborations among ITER, JET, and EAST have created open data tools and training programs, strengthening engineering capacity worldwide. These efforts also support fusion-compatible materials, vacuum systems, and power electronics that improve industrial plasma processing. A practical iritic testbed can demonstrate how fusion knowledge transfers to compact energy, materials science, and clean industrial innovation.
